title: Why ‘Heated Rivalry’ Received Zero Emmy Nominations
summary: “Heated Rivalry” is ineligible for any 2026 Emmy Award nominations. We break down the award show’s rules and explain why Connor Storrie did receive a nod.
story: “Heated Rivalry” launched a worldwide phenomenon when it first premiered in November 2025. But despite the TV series’ massive popularity, it won’t be taking home any awards when the 78th Emmy Awards airs this September.

The Television Academy announced its full list of nominees for the upcoming awards show on July 8. Each year, there are always surprises and snubs. But one of the hottest series of the 2025-2026 season was always guaranteed to be excluded from the list, and it comes down to the Emmy Awards specific eligibility rules.

One of “Heated Rivalry’s” breakout actors, though, did receive a nod at the 2026 Emmys. Connor Storrie, who plays Russian hockey player Ilya Rozanov, was nominated for outstanding guest actor in a comedy series for hosting “Saturday Night Live” in February. He faces Michael J. Fox, Brett Goldstein, Hamish Linklater, Christopher McDonald and Rob Reiner, who received a posthumous nomination for Season 4 of “The Bear.”
Why Is ‘Heated Rivalry’ Ineligible for Emmy Award Nominations?
One Emmy policy prevents the show from scoring a nomination.

According to the Emmys’ rules and procedures, foreign television production is ineligible “unless it is the result of a co-production (both financially and creatively) between U.S. and foreign partners, which precedes the start of production, and with a purpose to be shown on U.S. television.”

“Heated Rivalry,” based on Canadian author Rachel Reid’s 2019 romantic hockey novel of the same name, was produced in Canada. The TV adaptation, which was first announced in June 2025, is original to Crave, a Canadian streamer.
“This was a Canadian book. We’re Canadian producers,” creator Jacob Tierney told “CBS Mornings” in February.
The show was able to air in the U.S. when, nine days before its November premiere, HBO Max announced it had acquired the rights.

According to IMDB, the show’s country of origin is Canada. The website lists multiple production companies behind the show, including Bell Media, Bell Broadcast and New Media Fund, Accent Aigu Entertainment, Canada Media Fund, Crave and Sphere Abacus.

Tierney and “Heated Rivalry” co-creator Brendan Brady appeared on NPR’s “Planet Money” in February 2026 to discuss the show and its production process. Brady said the show was “made in the Canadian system,” which he described as “very different from the U.S.”
What Awards Is ‘Heated Rivalry’ Eligible For?

“Heated Rivalry” is eligible for the International Emmy Awards, per The Hollywood Reporter and Deadline, which will be held on Nov. 23, 2026, in New York City. Nominees will be announced in September.
Per the award’s website, the International Emmy Awards feature 16 award categories.

Even though “Heated Rivalry” isn’t eligible for the Emmy Awards, it has already won multiple accolades. At the 2026 Canadian Screen Awards, the show took home 16 awards including best drama series and best lead performer, drama series, for Hudson Williams.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Recalls the Prank She Did at 5 That Got Her Parents ‘So Mad’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager tried a prank call while she was a kid in the White House.
story: Like many kids, Jenna Bush Hager tried out a prank call or two. Only hers were to offices in the White House.

During TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on July 8, Jenna recalled the mischief she and her sister, Barbara Bush, got into as girls, when her grandfather George H. W. Bush was president of the United States.
“Barbara and I, we were 5, and we kept calling the vice president’s office,” Jenna admitted to Sheinelle.
She went on to re-enact her childhood shenanigans. “Where’s the president?” she asked in a stuttering baby voice.
Jenna then described the aftermath of when her father, George W. Bush, and mother, Laura Bush, realized what had happened.

“My parents came home, and we were actually at a friends house. I don’t know how we got the number,” Jenna explains. “My parents were so mad at us, we kept calling my grandpa’s office over and over again.”

The co-hosts then reacted to a moment Jenna got pranked. During an episode of ELLE’s “Phoning It In,” comedian Matt Rogers, who was Jenna’s co-host throughout 2025, pretended to be locked inside a 30 Rock dressing room. Rogers called Jenna for help, saying 9-1-1 was unresponsive.
Jenna said she completely fell for Rogers’ prank.
“I was like, ‘You’re calling 9-1-1 and they’re not answering?’ and then he’s like, ‘I’m scared!’ and I’m like, ‘Is he OK?’ I thought he had gone completely off the rails.”
Sheinelle did her share of prank calls, too. “If I hadn’t done any prank calls, then I hadn’t lived. I had a childhood!” she joked.

title: Laverne Cox Reveals the Heartbreaking Belief She Carried for Years: ‘I Was a Mistake’
summary: In the latest episode of Making Space, actress Laverne Cox opens up to Hoda Kotb about how she finally healed from childhood trauma, including abuse, bullying and shame.
story: From the outside, Laverne Cox, Emmy-winning actress, red-carpet fashion icon and LGBTQ+ advocate best known for playing Sophia Burset on Netflix’s “Orange Is the New Black,”  appears to embody confidence.
But behind the scenes, the actress says she spent years carrying a painful belief rooted in childhood — she believed she was “a mistake.”

During an emotional conversation with Hoda Kotb on the July 8 episode of the Making Space Podcast, Cox opened up about the shame that shaped her early life — and the moment she finally began to let it go.
“I was walking around feeling like I was a mistake,” she reveals to Kotb of her emotional state as a young child, which she carried with her into adulthood.
This shame, largely stemmed from her relationship with her mother: “I felt like this horrible burden. I felt unwanted, like I was a mistake who was ruining this woman’s life.”
She opens up to Hoda about being left at an orphanage, taken to conversion therapy, and being punished when she was bullied by other kids.
“I didn’t feel protected. I felt shamed. I felt judged. I felt terrified,” she says.
When her grandmother passed away, the shame became unbearable. Raised in the Christian church, Cox was taught that sexual thoughts about the same sex were a sin.

“My grandmother was up in heaven, and she couldn’t know that I was thinking these things. It was so much shame,” she explains. “It was like, ‘I can’t disappoint her, I can’t go to hell, this can’t be.’ It was not acceptable.”
The shame drove Cox to attempt suicide at age 11.
“When I woke up and I wasn’t dead, I [decided] I’m just gonna bury everything, and I’m gonna be perfect,” she says. “I shoved every feeling, everything down.”

She looked at middle school as her makeover. “That’ll be my identity, I’ll be the smart kid. I’ll keep doing my talent shows. I will be a straight-A student. I will be National Junior Honor Society. I will be perfect, and I will be really focused on being successful, so I can get out of Alabama,” she recalls “And then because my mother was a teacher, I felt like she would love me if I was a good student, if I didn’t cause any problems.”
Kotb reflects on how exhausting this perfectionism must have been.
“Exhausting is exactly the right word,” says Cox. “You’re second-guessing yourself, you’re constantly running things through a filter.”

title: Are There Female Minions? Co-Creator and Voice of Minions Explains
summary: Pierre Coffin shares why there hasn’t been female Minions and if there will be some in the future.
story: The Minions are back in the spotlight with “Minions & Monsters,” the seventh film in the “Despicable Me” franchise.

This time, James, a creative Minion with aspirations of becoming a filmmaker, teams up with friends Henry and Ed to make a monster movie. And as always, the comical yellow capsule-sized henchmen do what they do best: create havoc and bring the laughs.
As a new “Minions” film is released, it brings up the question: Are there female minions? “Minions & Monsters” director Pierre Coffin shares his answer.
“Last time I answered, I got into a lot of trouble,” Coffin, who is also the voice behind the Minions, jokes to TODAY.com.
In 2015, Coffin told The Wrap that because of their lack of intelligence, he “couldn’t imagine” there being female Minions.
“We talk about it all the time and I don’t know if we’re going to have an answer to that,” Coffin tells TODAY.com. “There’s no reason why it’s just males.”
Coffin co-created Minions along with character designer Eric Guillon and director Chris Renaud for 2010’s “Despicable Me.” The trio have since worked on the rest of the films.

“As we were making the first one, at some point we said to Steve Carell, voicing Gru, ‘Oh, just say hi to these guys as if they’re all the same, but you recognize each individual. So if you could just name them, like, Hey, Joe. Hey, Tim...,” he says, adding they preferred “very simple” names. “And so he came up with all that. He could have at that moment said, like, ‘Hey, Kelly. Hey, Clara.’ You know, ‘Lynn, Liz.’”
The creative team “didn’t question” the names at the moment, he says. “So it was... a decade later that someone came up with that question and said, ‘I don’t have an answer to that.’”
Coffin, however, adds, “but there might be in the future, though. Who knows?”
The director does say that he and the creative team have always envisioned the Minions as kids.

“It works magically,” he says. “It’s just them like fooling around, getting mad at each other, but two seconds later they’re friends again. It’s all about the expressive connection and how physical they are with each other. They’re kids.”

title: Meet the Cast of ‘Big Brother’ 2026: Who’s in Season 28?
summary: “Big Brother” has announced the houseguests for its upcoming Season 28. Meet the cast.
story: “Big Brother” fans, summer has officially arrived, which means it is time to meet the houseguests you’ll watch face the unexpected and compete for the next few months.

On July 7, “Big Brother” announced its Season 28 cast in a YouTube “Broveal” where fans watched a brief house tour before being introduced to the houseguests. Among the 14 contestants ready to form alliances, win Power of Vetoes and deceive are a rocket scientist, a MMA fighter and a “RuPaul’s Drag Race All Stars” alum.
The video began with host Julie Chen Moonves giving a sneak peek of the house.

“For Season 28, we’re throwing out all the rules of time and space and sending our houseguests on a journey unlike anything you’ve ever seen before,” Chen Moonves said. “History is about to be made. So buckle up, because we’re about to travel through time.”

She explained that time, including time travel, will be the theme for Season 28. After pointing out details in the living room, kitchen, lounge and more spots, it was time for the 14 houseguests to make an appearance. Each player mapped out some of their strategies and teased what viewers can expect from them.

But they are not the only players moving into the “Big Brother” house this season. CBS confirmed in a press release that more houseguests will be revealed during the show’s 90-minute premiere on Thursday, July 9, at 8 p.m. ET/ PT. The episode will also stream on Paramount+.

Two of the extra houseguests have already been revealed, one a reality television fan favorite and the other a “Big Brother” alum. “Survivor” Season 50 star Rick Devens will compete this season, Entertainment Weekly reported July 7. Devens originally competed on “Survivor: Edge of Extinction” before returning for the historic Season 50 that aired earlier this year.

Angela Murray, who competed on “Big Brother” Season 26, will make her return, according to Men’s Journal. The Utah real estate agent was evicted in sixth place, delighting and frustrating fans with her chaotic gameplay. She also was a contestant on “The Amazing Race” Season 38, where she competed with her daughter Lexi.
What can Devens, Murray and the rest of houseguests expect this “Big Brother” season?

A press release for Season 28 reads, “This new group of houseguests is stepping into a summer where nothing is as it seems, where every twist rewrites the rules, and where time becomes the ultimate twist.”

Following the premiere, fans will get to see how Devens and the other additional houseguests disrupt the game when the “Big Brother Live Feeds,” which show the players in real time 24/7, begin on Friday, July 10, at 9 p.m. ET/ 6 p.m. PT on Paramount+ and Pluto TV. title: ‘The Odyssey’ First Reactions: What Critics Are Saying About ‘The Most Must-See Theatrical Experience of Our Generation’
summary: Christopher Nolan’s epic summer blockbuster, “The Odyssey,” has just begun early screenings. Find what critics have to say ahead of the July 17 release.
story: Tickets for Christopher Nolan’s epic blockbuster “The Odyssey” have been sold out for months as fans eagerly await the July 17 release of the filmmaker’s most ambitious project to date.

But is all the hype worth it? If social media reactions to early screenings are any indication, “The Odyssey” is about to become the summer’s biggest movie — if not one of the most iconic films of the year.

Filmed in 91 days, “The Odyssey” was shot entirely in IMAX in locations across the world, including Greece, Italy, Morocco, Iceland and Scotland. Written and directed by Nolan, the 2-hour, 53-minute epic features an all-star cast led by Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, John Leguizamo, Lupita Nyong’o, Samantha Norton, Zendaya and Charlize Theron.
For those who slept through middle-school English, “The Odyssey” is based on Homer’s epic, 12,000 line poem by the same name, thought to have been penned sometime during the 7th or 8th century BCE.

Steeped in Greek mythology, the story tells the tale of Odysseus (Damon), a Greek king who, after conquering Troy via the Trojan Horse, begins the long voyage to Ithaca to reunite with wife, Penelope (Hathaway), and son, Telemachus (Holland).
It’s an emotional and physical saga that takes Odysseus and his beleaguered crew across raging oceans, through the fires of Hades and into the caves of monsters, before reaching its epic conclusion.
Joining the ranks of films like “Lord of the Rings” and “Lawrence of Arabia,” see below to find out what early critics are saying about Nolan’s “The Odyssey.”
Variety

After seeing an early screening of “The Odyssey,” Variety senior editor, Jazz Tangcay, posted, “I have seen Christopher Nolan’s #TheOdyssey, and it is an astonishing achievement. A triumphant, spectacular epic. The performances from Tom Holland, Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, John Leguizamo, Robert Pattinson and Lupita Nyong’o are genuinely grand. And for some, truly, the best performances of their career!”

In a follow-up post, Tangcay continued by raving that “The Odyssey” is a “work of art,” saying that Nolan did an “incredible job” of bringing Homer’s masterpiece to the big screen and the result is “breathtaking.”
“He has outdone himself. You could feel the passion in his storytelling. You feel the passion in the crafts and the acting.”
Screenrant
Liam Crowley of ScreenRant posts, “The Odyssey is the most must-see theatrical experience of our generation. An absolute redefinition of the word epic and a new gold standard for blockbuster cinema.”

Though Crowley cites several memorable performances, he singles out Hathaway’s as being a “Oscars win lock.” Saying that the film is Nolan’s “crown jewel,” the ScreenRant critic raves that “The Odyssey” is “paced to perfection” and that each act of the blockbuster could be a “best picture nomination.”
Empire Magazine
Nick de Semlyen of London’s Empire Magazine posted on X and said that “The Odyssey” is “rich, propulsive, deeply emotional filmmaking” and wrote that the cast had “too many standouts to mention.”
Even so, he flagged performances by Elliot Page, John Leguizamo and Robert Pattinson as being among the most memorable.
After seeing the film twice, de Semlyen said his second viewing was “even more satisfying.”
The Independent

Jacob Stolworthy, chief film and TV correspondent for The Independent, posted on X that Nolan’s film has about “triple the number of huge set pieces” than any of the director’s previous films and that “every single one of them is breathtaking.”

Stolworthy also said that Nolan used “visual trickery” in a way no one has seen him do before. Stolworthy’s only complaint? That the sets were so good, it left him wanting more, thus making a re-watch a must.
Finally, of the cast, Stolworthy wrote that it was “stacked,” with each of the high-profile actors delivering, especially Holland, Norton and Himesh Patel, who plays Odysseus’ second-in-command.
Collider

Collider editor-in-chief Steven Weintraub posted his initial reaction to the blockbuster, writing, “I’m really blown away by this film. Everything from the flawless performances to the way Nolan embraces the supernatural is just perfect.”
Weintraub continued by writing that the best way to see the film is in IMAX, calling it a “jaw dropping experience.”
Erik Davis of Fandango and Rotten Tomatoes

TV and movie critic Erik Davis, who contributes to both Fandango and Rotten Tomatoes, hailed “The Odyssey” as a “triumph” on X, and said that the film was a “crowning achievement” from one of “the great filmmakers of our time.”
Calling it “breathtaking,” Davis said the blockbuster is the “must-see cinematic event of the summer” and, perhaps, even the year. “I can’t wait to watch it again,” he concluded.
Time Out
Phil de Semlyen, global film editor for Time Out, added his glowing review to the list with a post on X.

“Believe the hype(rbole): The Odyssey is that film. Dense but accessible, packed with career-best work from the stacked cast — Samantha Morton is extraordinary — it’s a dizzying mix of craft and spectacle that’s built to last.”

He continued by writing, “A chilling vision of brutalised men seeing themselves in the eyes of women, a study of leadership and an old-school sweeping adventure tale. Even the cyclops got me in the feels. There’s even a few laughs, too. Go see. Twice.”
“The Odyssey” is produced and distributed by Universal, a subsidiary of NBCUniversal, TODAY’s parent company.

title: Romantic Drama ‘Voicemails for Isabelle’ Is a Love Letter to Sisterhood. The Director Explains Its Inspiration
summary: “Voicemails for Isabelle” director, writer and star Leah McKendrick tells TODAY.com the inspiration behind the Netflix romantic-comedy.
story: Netflix’s tearjerker “Voicemails for Isabelle” is making audiences want to hug their loved ones a little tighter.

The Netflix romantic comedy stars Zoey Deutch as Jill, an aspiring chef who starts leaving messages to her sister Izzy (Ciara Bravo) after she dies. Unbeknownst to Jill, her voicemails, filled with hilarious and embarrassing stories about her day, are being listened to by a real estate agent in Austin, Texas, named Wes, played by Nick Robinson, who inherited Izzy’s phone number.

The film’s depiction of love and loss against the backdrop of San Francisco has captured viewers’ and social media users’ attention, landing the No. 1 film spot on Netflix for the week of June 22 through June 28.
It seemed the film became a success overnight, and no one is more shocked than director and screenwriter Leah McKendrick, who also stars in the movie as Wes’ friend Breeda.

“You don’t ever really know how the public will respond,” McKendrick tells TODAY.com. “I will say, we did a test screening, and a lot of people were leaving crying. Again, I just wasn’t sure if maybe it was because we were in a theater or, I don’t know. I just didn’t expect it.”

“I will tell you that I’m the biggest dreamer, and I have been born with impossible dreams and high visions. It’s a blessing, and it’s a curse,” she adds. “But even I did not expect this level of love and emotional reaction to the film, so I am humbled and I’m honored.”
McKendrick, whose relationship with her own sister inspired the screenplay, originally penned the script over eight years ago. One of the first people to read the draft was her sibling.

Below, she opens up about more ways her art imitates life, including the connections between her upbringing and Jill’s journey to find her place in San Francisco. She also reveals why she personally wrote to Taylor Swift to ask to use two of her songs on the soundtrack and why the world needs rom-coms right now.

title: ‘Love on the Spectrum’ Star Connor Tomlinson Debuts New Relationship
summary: Connor Tomlinson just went public with a new girlfriend after his breakup with Georgie Harris was shown in Season 3 of Love on the Spectrum.
story: Connor Tomlinson has a new special someone in his life, and he’s ready to share her with the world.
The “Love on the Spectrum” star introduced his girlfriend to his Instagram followers in a short and sweet video posted on July 6.
In the clip, the Netflix star lies down on a pool chair as the words “Life with her” appear in the frame. Connor sits up and a woman leans in to kiss him on the cheek, then they both smile.
“Hard launch 🚀 @sarahsiebert4204 ♥️,” he captioned the post.
Both Connor and Sarah shared the post on their respective Instagram accounts.
Connor offered further insight into their budding relationship in the comments section, writing, “Sarah and I are just boyfriend & girlfriend and for now that’s good enough for us ❤️‍🔥.”
“Love on the Spectrum” alums like Tanner Smith and Subodh Garg sent him their well wishes in the comments section.
“I’m SO HAPPY FOR YOU, Connor!!!👏👏👏,” Tanner wrote.
“Yay congratulations Connor!” Subodh commented.
On “Love on the Spectrum,” Connor was vocal about his preferences, including that he preferred brunettes. He was once indignant when his mother wanted to introduce him to a blonde.
Since his new girlfriend has blonde highlights, many fans of the show playfully teased Connor in the comments section.
“But she’s a blonde!?!?” one commented.
Another wrote, “She’s far from blonde, people!! She is light brown with some highlights.”
When one fan asked if Connor is the same age as his new girlfriend, he replied, writing, “She is five days older.”
In April, Connor announced his decision to leave “Love on the Spectrum” after three seasons and told Variety he had “chosen to pass the torch to the next person who can make it as big as me.”
Connor met his former girlfriend Georgie Harris in Season 3 of the reality show. They broke up in Season 4, which aired earlier this year.
His mother, Lise Smith, spoke about the decision to keep the breakup discussion off camera in an episode of her podcast, “Talk to Me Sis.”
“I felt like this was a private moment that didn’t need to be consumed,” Smith said.
She also revealed that Connor was “the initiator of the breakup.”
“I don’t necessarily know that Georgie saw that coming ... I don’t think she wanted to break up. I’m not sure,” she said.
In the end, Smith said Connor was seeking a more “adult connection” than Georgie. However, she said they remain friends and “wish nothing but the best for each other.”

title: EXCLUSIVE: OWN Announces New Spinoff Show ‘Put A Ring on It: Cheathab’
summary: OWN has revealed a new reality show that will put three couples through an unimaginable test. See TODAY.com’s exclusive trailer for “Put a Ring on It: Cheathab.”
story: OWN has revealed a new reality show that will put three couples through an unimaginable test.
“Put a Ring on It: Cheathab,” adds a twist to the original series, “Put a Ring on It.”

The flagship show introduces viewers to three long-term couples who, with the help of love, dating and relationship coach Dr. Stacii Jae Johnson, go through an experiment to find out if they are truly meant for each other and ready to take the next step in their relationships. But in “Cheathab,” a play on cheating and rehab, the new series will follow three couples who have faced issues of infidelity in the past.

In the upcoming show, three couples will move into a Miami-based “Cheathab House” where they will have to confront their trust issues. While living in the “Cheathab House,” they will date other people, including former flings and past lovers who might be the source of tension in their current relationships.
Dr. Stacii will guide each couple on their journey as they determine if they can resolve their problems and move forward, or if they want to call it quits for good.

“As old feelings resurface and new temptations emerge, the couples must confront painful truths and decide whether they can rebuild trust and commit to a future together,” a press release about the new series reads. “By the end of the experiment, they face a life-changing decision: finally ‘put a ring on it’ and build a life together or walk away for good.”
TODAY.com can exclusively reveal a first–look of the series, which teases the couples struggling with the “radical honesty” Dr. Stacii wants them to tackle.
“Y’all are going to find out if the connection you had was more than just a fling,” Dr. Stacii says in a voiceover. She is also seen advising one couple to change their bad habits.
Elsewhere, one woman is serenaded by a man and sheds a few tears. “This is what I desire from my man,” she says.
Another clip shows a contestant telling Dr. Stacii, “She needs to carry herself better because I will carry myself out of here and be happy.”
The final moments of the trailer reveal one couple might leave the experiment engaged.
“Put a Ring on It: Cheathab” premieres Friday, July 31, at 9 p.m. ET/PT on OWN. The show will then move to its regular time of Fridays at 8 p.m. ET/PT starting Aug. 14.

Speaking about the new series, OWN President Tina Perry said in a statement, “OWN has long embraced relationship programming centered on love, growth and emotional truth. ‘Put a Ring on It: Cheathab’ is now supercharged with a bold new lens on love, exploring what happens when both partners have crossed the line and must decide whether trust can truly be rebuilt.”

In addition to advising each couple, Dr. Stacii will also lead workshops that will help the couples rebuild their intimacy and trust. Get to know the three pairs who are embarking on this experiment together, below.
Meet the Couples of ‘Put A Ring on It: Cheathab’

Dominique and Travis have been able to navigate a long-distance relationship thanks to their emotional connection and late-night conversations. But, after Travis revealed to Dominique that he had a fling in Vegas, the two have not been the same. While Dominique is looking for commitment and security, Travis wants her to have faith in him.

Mia and Jarron met on Facebook in 2022 and began dating despite living on opposite sides of the country. They overcame the distance between Los Angeles and Fort Lauderdale by bonding over their faith. However, Mia started to doubt him after learning that Jarron had been messaging and sleeping with other women. She then turned to one of his friends for support. They are both wondering if they can put their pain behind them.

Mi-Mi and Joshua were introduced to each other by a mutual friend and fell in love. But Joshua later cheated with his ex and Mi-Mi reconnected with her ex and developed an emotional connection. Despite their problems, Joshua has proposed twice. Mi-Mi won’t accept until she knows the trust between them has been restored.

title: AI ‘Actor’ Tilly Norwood Lands First Movie Role. Its Creator Responds to the Criticism
summary: AI-generated actor Tilly Norwood will star in an upcoming movie, prompting its creator to justify the technology that has come under fire.
story: Tilly Norwood, the AI-generated “actor” whose creation alone sparked backlash, could soon be coming to a theater near you. The company that created Tilly has announced it will star in a full-length feature.

Particle 6, the studio that created Tilly, is making a film called “Misaligned,” marking the first time the AI character will star in a movie. The film, which will take place in the so-called “Tillyverse,” is a coming of age story about a girl AI bot.

“Misaligned” will star Tilly in a “hybrid production with traditional film and TV professionals — such as directors, writers and editors — working alongside AI specialists, with AI training and mentorship built into the production itself,” the company said, according to NBC News.

“Our work this year has proven something we suspected all along,” Tilly’s creator, Eline Van der Velden, said in a statement, according to NBC News. “AI can support premium narrative filmmaking, but only with substantial amounts of human craft, skill, judgment and time. That’s not a limitation of the technology. That’s the point.”
Speaking with NBC News’ Liz Kreutz, Van der Velden denied that Tilly’s role in “Misaligned” takes work away from human actors.
“Because we would never be making a feature film, so we would never have been casting,” she said.
But she said Tilly’s creation could mark a tipping point, ushering in more and more usage of AI in film.
“I don’t disagree with any of that, right? I do think a lot of films will be made using AI, but I don’t think it will stop live action at all,” Van der Velden said.
Tilly was unveiled in 2025, sparking criticism from actors, SAG-AFTRA and other industry professionals.

“Does it disappoint me? I don’t know how to quite answer it, other than to say how terrifying this is,” Emily Blunt told Variety in September 2025 before the publication showed her a picture of Tilly.
“No, are you serious? That’s an AI?” she said. “Good lord, we’re screwed. That is really, really scary, Come on, agencies, don’t do that. Please stop. Please stop taking away our human connection.”
SAG-AFTRA, the union which represents actors, said it was “opposed to the replacement of human performers by synthetics” in a statement in September 2025.
“SAG-AFTRA believes creativity is, and should remain, human-centered,” the union said.
Van der Velden previously told the UK’s Broadcast International  her goal is for Tilly “to be the next Scarlett Johansson or Natalie Portman.”

Some in Hollywood appear to see AI’s potential. Academy Award winner Matthew McConaughey has licensed his voice for AI-generated bilingual content with ElevenLabs, where he is an investor. Demi Moore said during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, “AI is here” and encouraged Hollywood to “find ways in which we can work with it,” per Variety.

Val Kilmer, who died in 2025, will be re-created through AI in the upcoming movie “As Deep As the Grave” with the blessing of his estate. Kilmer’s daughter, Mercedes Kilmer, said her father was hoping to lay a foundation for how the technology can be used.

“My dad was very passionate (that) this is the time, before these laws are written, to make sure that there’s a structure for compensation, to make sure that actors get paid on par with what they would get paid if they were physically doing it, and if it creates more jobs in that way, that’s wonderful,” Mercedes Kilmer told TODAY in April.
While the technology exists, it isn’t yet clear if moviegoers will be interested in a movie made by AI.
“I think it’ll depend on whether the product is good,” Bloomberg News managing editor and “Screentime” newsletter author Lucas Shaw told TODAY.

Moviegoers should not expect to see Tilly in “Misaligned” anytime soon. Van der Velden said the film is in the early stages of production, and most likely won’t be finished until next year at the earliest.

title: Terry Bradshaw Gets Candid with Craig About Going to Therapy Before Marrying Wife Tammy
summary: Terry Bradshaw, NFL Hall of Famer, has been happily wed to wife Tammy Bradshaw since 2014 and calls marrying her a “grand slam.”
story: Terry Bradshaw, NFL Hall of Famer, has been happily wed to wife Tammy Bradshaw since 2014 and calls marrying her a “grand slam.”

But Bradshaw, 77, also said he knows “exactly why” he got divorced three times before Tammy, he told Craig Melvin on the July 7 episode of the “Glass Half Full” podcast. So with wife Tammy, he took extra precaution to not repeat the same mistakes.
“I know exactly why I married those women, and I only know that because I spent three years in therapy. Seriously, to try to figure out what the hell is wrong with me,” Bradshaw told Craig.

“I realized after my third divorce ... I started thinking about my first wife, and I went, ‘I wasn’t in love with her.’ I didn’t realize I had been dealing with depression, and I would make terrible decisions in the bottom of depression,” he added.
Bradshaw said he realized his first three marriages “were just alike,” making him the common denominator.
“It wasn’t them, it was me. And I started working on me, and that’s what changed my life,” he said.

He turned to a counselor, a preacher and a psychologist until he found a therapist who could help, he told Craig. When things started to get serious with Tammy, he tried to not let his emotions get ahead of him.
“I figured it out, and so I dated Tammy, fell in love, and said, ‘Not so fast, Terry, let’s make sure here,’” he said.
They waited 12 years before finally tying the knot in 2014.
Since though, the couple has traveled together, launched a family cookbook and supported one another through difficult times, including Bradshaw’s cancer journey, TODAY previously reported.
Now, his marriage with Tammy is what he’s most proud of, he said.

“I finally got it right. Do you know what it’s like to marry someone who is your partner, that you would rather play golf with her, you’d rather fish with her, you’d rather do everything in the world with her?” he said. “I never thought that my buddies would take second place, but they do.”

title: He’s Stuart, Bob and Kevin. Meet the Man Behind the Minions
summary: Pierre Coffin, the voice of all the Minions and the director of the most recently movie “Minions and Monsters,” opens up in an interview.
story: WHEN PIERRE COFFIN is asked who his favorite Minion is, he instantly replies Stuart.

“It’s Stuart. Stuart is me,” the director and co-writer of “Minions & Monsters” tells TODAY.com, referring to the one-eyed, laid back, yet mischievous Minion with hair parted in the middle. In fact, Stuart also plays the ukulele, just like Coffin.

“I started playing the ukulele and I thought, ‘Oh, I should give that to that Minion.’ So Stuart plays the ukulele. And Stuart doesn’t care about anything, I don’t care about anything,” Coffin says, adding that Stuart is the rebellious teenager compared to big brother Kevin and innocent, naive and lovable Bob.

But the thing is, Coffin really is Stuart — and Kevin, and Bob, and Dave, and Otto and Gus. The list goes on. And that’s because Coffin is also the man behind the voice of the Minions — literally all the Minions.

Minions were first introduced in 2010’s “Despicable Me,” an animated film that followed supervillain Gru (voiced by Steve Carell), who, on his quest to steal the moon, adopts three orphan girls. Stuart, Bob and Kevin, along with the rest of the silly capsule-shaped henchmen, would go on to become stars of their own. They captured the hearts of many with their playful antics, their love for their “big boss” and going bonkers for bananas.

The franchise has since successfully expanded with four “Despicable Me” films and now three “Minions” spinoffs. In 2024, Universal announced that the “Despicable Me” franchise crossed $5 billion globally.
The latest film, “Minions & Monsters,” out now, has Coffin returning to not only voice and co-write, but also be the sole director of the film.

“It made it certainly more fun,” Coffin says about helming the film. “From the moment I knew that I had to write it, I was becoming highly responsible of the outcome. So when you accumulate the roles of writer, director and voice actor for all the main characters, you start having fun, for sure.”
“But,” he adds, “(I’m) a little bit scared of this moment when the movie is going to come out — and hopefully didn’t goof things up a little too much.”
“Minions & Monsters” earned $160 million worldwide in its debut week, according to The Associated Press.
IT TAKES A VILLAGE and many years to produce an animated movie, three years specifically for “Minions & Monsters,” Coffin says.

At first hesitant to return to the franchise due to the extensive work, Coffin became intrigued with the idea of Minions in a 1920s backdrop during the era of the silent film, with hopes of creating their own monster movie.

And that’s where viewers discover James, a creative and passionate Minion who loves to draw and tell stories. He, along with pals Henry and Ed, set their sights on bringing his horror film to life — and it definitely comes to life when monsters are summoned and try to take over Hollywood.
“I wanted it to be fresh, not like another ‘Minions’ movie,” Coffins says, explaining that setting the film around the invention of sound made for a unique perspective.
So how are the scripts drafted when it comes to Minionese, the nonsensical, gibberish language the Minions speak?
On “Minions,” writer Brian Lynch wrote Minionese as gibberish, Coffin says. “But it was hard to read because I didn’t know what the gibberish was.”

“So then he started writing in English,” he continues. “We sort of established that principle where he’d write the dialogues in English, and I would do whatever I wanted in the edit stage or when I had to do the voices.”
“We spent at least a year out of three trying to figure out a way of writing this thing, trying to make sense of it,” Coffin says.
Challenges also arose when it came to translating the films in other languages. He estimates that he uses “at least half a dozen” languages or “slightly beyond” to create Minionese.

“Apparently I say a lot of swear words in all these different countries without knowing,” he says. “I’m thinking I’m inventing words, but I’m saying words that are highly offensive. So ... I spent a week correcting those mistakes.”
He then finds other words to switch out and spends an additional two weeks or so “redoing voices (for) different countries.”
For instance, he says, South American audiences prefer “grande jeje” rather than “big boss.”
“So I redo all that, and I spent two weeks redoing all these voices for everyone.”
COFFIN DOES NOT speak Minionese. “I have to write it down.”

“For one thing, I’m a very bad actor, and the second thing, I’m a very bad improviser,” he says, explaining that the secret to understanding Minionese is “not in the words I’m saying, but more in the melody.”
The inflection and the tone, which he described as “little music,” is how Minionese is understood.

“It’s just that little music, the tone at which I perform, so I just go literally, ‘blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah,’” he says with his tone going up and down. “And then see if that means what I’m hoping the thing means, and then I replaced all the ‘blah, blah, blahs’ with words, food or famous pop stars or stuff like that.”

He says that because they have the “gift of time,” they’re hoping audiences understand what they’re trying to express. “But you’re not 100% sure. So you have to test that,” he says, and if it doesn’t work, “We got to go back to the writing table.”

Getting into the technical part of it, he doesn’t use a filter to voice the Minions, “Because it destroys the quality of the sound.” Instead, he records his voice in slow motion and when played back at real speed, he’s sped up. “But pitched up also,” he says. “And that’s when the magic happens ... But most of the time it’s me just trying at different speeds and different tones.”

When asked if he hopes to pass the torch to someone else to voice the Minions, he replies, “Oh, sure, yeah,” explaining that he’s not keeping the little guys to himself. “It’s natural for me to do it, particularly when you’re making and telling the stories. It feels like the two are linked together because, in some cases, you can come up with the idea and then I start voicing it.”
FOR “MINIONS & MONSTERS,” Coffin embraced the idea of friendship, connection and inclusivity.
Ed, for example, is another Minion that Coffin really embraced. He liked the idea of incorporating a hearing impaired Minion that expressed himself in sign language.

“But he expresses himself with the same gibberish as the Minions, which I’m hoping people will notice,” he says, adding that the creative team had a counselor to help. “Because sign language is also a per country thing. So (the counselor) sort of mixed it up, so that hopefully in all the countries it’ll work at a specific level.”
It’s those tiny but specific details that Coffin really enjoys when creating a “Despicable Me” franchise film.
When crafting James, Coffin knew he was an artist. Meanwhile, Henry “likes having a life, but his main character trait is that he loves his buddy,” Coffin says.

As for how you illustrate friendship in visual form? Coffin likens the Minions to kids. “And from the moment you depict them as kids, as we have always done by the way, it works magically,” Coffin says.

“It’s just them fooling around, getting mad at each other, but two seconds later they’re friends again. It’s all about the expressive connection and how physical they are with each other. They’re kids.”

title: Nobody Made Reece Weaver Quit the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders
summary: Reece Weaver opens up about quitting the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders.
story: The only thing scarier than joining the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders is quitting the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders.

At the end of Season 3 of “America’s Sweethearts,” the Netflix reality series following the squad through its annual audition process, Reece Weaver decided to hang up her pompoms after just three seasons with DCC.

“It was more scary to leave, because it’s like, ‘Oh gosh, now what do I do?’ I’m jumping into the real world. I don’t know what is next. I think it was more of the unknowns that were scary,” she tells TODAY.com.
For viewers, the move was genuinely surprising. Weaver, who has a classical studio background, was a breakout star for Season 1, which followed the selection for the 2023-2024 football season.
She retired during a conversation with director of the DCC Kelli Finglass and choreographer Judy Trammell shown in Episode 7.

“That was honestly one of the scariest days of my life,” Weaver says. “My biggest fear was, I wanted to eloquently share everything that was on my heart. Right before I walked in, (my husband) Will (Allman) was praying with me, and I just kept saying, ‘Speak through me, Lord. Just speak through me.’ I was scared to not have the words.”

Weaver had been “wrestling” with the decision all season, she says. After three years, cheering with the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders felt “comfortable.” The cheerleaders had pushed to raise their salaries significantly since Weaver signed on and she knows she “would have enjoyed” more time on the squad.
But she says she was ready for more.
“I wanted to encourage others, that if they felt like they were being pulled, to take a leap of faith. I wanted to hopefully inspire them to do so and not be scared of it,” she says.
She expected fear and uncertainty after quitting. What she didn’t expect, however, was the feedback from people who doubted whether the decision was hers at all.

After “America’s Sweethearts” aired, viewers speculated about the reason behind her retirement. Was it the high ankle sprain she suffered during her third season? Or was it pressure from her husband, Will Allman?
“It’s frustrating,” Weaver says of the speculation. “I have the most incredible husband, who is so supportive, and I’m 100% healthy and could totally do another season.”
She emphasizes that Allman would have supported her “no matter what,” which makes the rumors especially “sad.”
“He made it extremely clear to me that it had to be my decision. I’m so grateful for that,” she says. “All he wants to do is support my dreams.”
Since leaving the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders, Weaver and Allman have gone back to their hometown of Tuscaloosa, Alabama. But she hasn’t settled into her new normal yet.
“I wish I could tell you exactly what it looks like, but I have not spent more than three days in our new home at a time,” she says. “Life has been so busy, just in a different way.”
Her plans, though, include “falling back in love” with the type of studio dance she did when she was younger. She’s also taken up singing lessons.
“I actually put on my dream board for 2026 that I want to do something that is really hard for me, and I want to get good at it. I didn’t know it was going to be singing at the time,” she says.
She says Broadway is a dream of hers, but so is staying grounded in Alabama.

“My friends say, ‘You’re literally living the Hannah Montana life.’ You’re traveling but going back home to your roots. Being centered with your community, while also living this ambitious, fun, kind of glamorized life,” she says.
“I still want to continue to dance and perform and do all the things, while also probably one day building a chicken coop in our backyard. That would be very Hannah Montana.”

title: Who Caught Taylor Swift’s Bouquet? Her Connection to Groom Travis Kelce
summary: Ashley Smith, a sister of Travis Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs teammate Trey Smith, caught Taylor Swift’s bouquet after she and Kelce married.
story: Travis Kelce is used to catching passes, but it’s a throw from his bride that may have one woman feeling lucky.

Ashley Smith, sister of Kelce’s Kansas City Chiefs teammate Trey Smith, said on Instagram that she caught Taylor Swift’s bouquet after the “Opalite” singer and Kelce got married. Their July 3 ceremony at New York City’s Madison Square Garden may be one of the most high profile weddings in history. Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce called “magical,” while other guests said it was a “pinch-me moment.”
Smith may have had her own pinch-me moment by catching the bouquet, potentially transforming 2026’s cruel summer into her love story.
What Did Ashley Smith Say About Catching the Bouquet?
Smith is hoping there’s some magic in the bouquet she caught.
“Celebrated an Enchanting Love S(T&T)ory 🤍✨🤍 And somehow…I ended up catching Tay Tay’s bouquet. 💐” she captioned a series of photos of her and her brother on Instagram July 5.
“So here’s to believing it’s bringing a lifetime of love, luck, and laughter my way,” she added. “Congratulations, Taylor & Travis! Cheers to forever T&T!”
Who Are Trey and Ashley Smith?

Trey Smith, 27, is a Jackson, Tennessee, native who plays guard on the offensive line for the Chiefs. He’s been with the team since they drafted him out of the University of Tennessee in 2021 in the sixth round, capping off a collegiate career in which he was a four-year starter.

Ashley Smith, meanwhile, has carved her own path in the NFL. In April, she wrote on Instagram that she wrapped up working at the league office. Her LinkedIn profile still lists her job as manager, player engagement, at the NFL.

“Taking time to reflect on this chapter, I am just incredibly grateful. Grateful for the opportunity to serve both current and former players through personal and professional development,” she wrote on Instagram.
She said she worked five Super Bowls, the draft, Pro Bowl and more high-profile events while with the NFL.
“I had a front row seat to some of the biggest moments in sports, but what I will cherish most are the people,” she wrote.

“The players I had the honor of serving are some of the most elite athletes in the world, but even better human beings. The colleagues across all 32 clubs are some of the brightest and most dedicated minds in football,” she added. “I am thankful for the opportunity to pour into others, to build, to lead, and to grow. I pray that the work I did continues to impact not only the players I worked with, but those who will come after them. Forever grateful for this chapter.”
Ashley Smith Is One of Her Brother’s Biggest Cheerleaders
Trey Smith re-signed with the Chiefs in 2025 for $94 million over four years, a record for a guard. That prompted his sister to think about his journey to becoming a standout football player.

“Losing Mom when you were just 15 was a blow none of us were prepared for. I saw how deeply it affected you, but I also saw how you kept going — how you turned pain into purpose,” she wrote on Instagram.
She reflected on more “tests” he faced in his career, such as suffering blood clots in his lungs in college.

“So many counted you out. So many thought you’d never play again,” she wrote. “But you made a promise to Mom to finish what you started, and you did just that — getting your degree and showing the world what true resilience looks like.”

“While you’ve often looked to me for direction, I’ve often looked to you for inspiration,” she added. Words can’t fully express how much your heart, your resilience, your faith, and your fight have impacted me. You’ve shown me what it means to persevere, to rise with grace, and to honor God through it all.”

title: Over 140 Celebrities Attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s Wedding: Everyone We Know
summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce were married July 3. Here’s a list of all the celebrities who attended.
story: The stars were aligned (literally) at Madison Square Garden this Independence Day weekend for the marriage of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce.
Swift and Kelce announced their engagement in August 2025. A few weeks later, Swift revealed how she was approaching crafting her wedding guest list.

“I think the only stressful weddings are the ones where you have a small amount, and people are on the bubble,” Swift said on “The Graham Norton Show” in October. “You have to evaluate or assess your relationship with them to see if they should be there. I’m not going to do that.”

It seems she kept to her word. A source who landed an invite told NBC News that around 1,100 people were expected to attend the July 3 ceremony. Meanwhile, an “intimate” gathering the night before welcomed around 100 guests, the New York Times reported.
Between these two events, there was quite the roundup of Hollywood household names, stars of the sports world and everyone in between.
Read on for some notable guests to the nuptials:
Swift and Kelce’s Families
In a statement announcing Swift and Kelce’s marriage, their representatives said the “the ceremony joined both families together.”
The newlyweds chose not to have bridesmaids or groomsmen, but Jason Kelce served as his brother’s best man, and Austin Swift was his sister’s “man of honor.”
Other key family members in attendance included Travis Kelce’s parents, Ed and Donna Kelce, and Taylor Swift’s parents, Scott and Andrea Swift.
Over the holiday weekend, Donna Kelce gave her first public comment about the wedding, calling it “magical.”
Taylor Swift’s aunt Robin Gentry was also in attendance and told reporters after the wedding, “they cried, and they laughed, and they danced, and they hugged and they kissed.”
Abigail Anderson
Anderson and Swift have been friends since childhood. In one of Swift’s earlier songs, “Fifteen,” she sings about the moment they met.
Anderson wore a dress with a floral corset and chocolate brown silk skirt — and twinned with Laura Kruk, fiancée of NFL player JuJu Smith-Schuster.
Adam Sandler
Swift and Kelce’s wedding was officiated by “friend” Adam Sandler, representatives for the couple said in a press release.
Andy Reid, head coach of the Kansas City Chiefs, gave a glimpse into what it was like having the comedian as an officiant.

“Adam Sandler (did) a phenomenal job with the ceremony,” Reid told CNN. “Just how he went about bringing a little bit of humor but also sensitivity to what was going on, to a lot of different types of people from a lot of different types of worlds, and bringing them all together.”
Karlie Kloss
Karlie Kloss was spotted in a gold strapless gown alongside husband Joshua Kushner just hours before the MSG doors opened.
Kloss and Swift were close amid Swift’s “1989” album era, notably taking a trip to Big Sur together in 2014.

Years later, fans started to point to an alleged falling out once the two were spotted together less frequently. The “Eras Tour,” however, made way for the first public connection between the two, as Kloss was seen dancing in the audience of Swift’s final Los Angeles stop.
Selena Gomez

Selena Gomez and Swift were brought together by the power of The Jonas Brothers. The two have publicly supported each other over the years, including at Gomez’s own wedding to Benny Blanco in October.
In 2020, Gomez said she was the muse for Swift’s song “Dorothea” from “Evermore.”
Paul McCartney and Stevie Nicks
Rolling Stone first reported that Stevie Nicks, a longtime mentor of Swift, would possibly be a guest and a performer.
Two guests who attended the wedding later told NBC News that Nicks and Paul McCartney performed at the reception — though Swift herself did not.
